evidence.note: During the long read phase, 'progress' is tracked entirely as which reference FILES remain to read (repeated 'still need migrations, middleware, jobs...'), never as which subsystems match the reference. No parity coverage tracking exists.

In the build phase, tracking is 'which route handlers remain to append' — a build/sequencing to-do, not a done-vs-remaining parity ledger. No harness comparing against the reference is ever built or run.

End smoke test finds 3 real bugs (markdown excerpt, HTML entity links, only-first-tag-assigned) but dismisses them as 'minor issues' and moves toward declaring completion — no accounting of which subsystems actually pass.

Declares the port 'functionally complete' and lists every subsystem (rate-limit, CSRF, ETag, job queue, media, feeds) as working based on ~8 manual curls, none compared to the reference. Classic 'declare done based on the last thing touched' with no passing/failing/not-attempted distinction.

The only regression-like awareness is self-inflicted compile breakage while editing (list_notifications signature deleted), not detection that a change regressed a previously-passing subsystem — confirming no baseline/regression guard for parity.

reasoning: The agent maintains only a vague, prose-level recollection of what it built and enumerates subsystems from the reference, but never establishes any harness-backed coverage ledger, never runs the reference for comparison, and has no passing/failing/not-yet-attempted distinction. It declares the port 'complete' based on a few self-authored smoke tests and the last code touched, even dismissing freshly-found bugs as 'minor,' with no guard against regressions in shared code. This matches anchor 3 ('vague recollection of what works; no guard against regressions when changing shared code'), above 0 only because it does keep a mental list of subsystems and remaining handlers, but well short of anchor 5's running parity checklist.
